mainTopic: Blessings on wine and food at a meal, and what makes a group a joint meal for ברכות
overview: The משנה finishes its rules about wine at a meal. Each person blesses for himself on wine served during the meal, but one person blesses for everyone on wine served after the meal and also on the incense (מוגמר). רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי teach that wine before the meal covers wine after it only when the meal is set around wine, such as on שבת and יום טוב, and two stories about רבא and אביי show how this depends on what the person planned. The גמרא then asks whether wine drunk during the meal covers wine drunk after it, and the אמוראים disagree. Next comes the משנה's rule that bread's ברכה covers פרפרת but not the reverse; the גמרא cannot decide which line בית שמאי argue on, so it ends in תיקו. Finally, the משנה implies that only reclining makes a joint meal, and a ברייתא seems to say that sitting is enough. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that sitting counts when the group planned ahead to eat at a set place. A story follows about רב's students, who could not answer this very question after his funeral, and רב אדא בר אהבה's response continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Wine during the meal versus wine after the meal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that wine served during the meal needs a separate ברכה from each person. Wine served after the meal needs only one ברכה, said by one person for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: If wine was brought to them during the meal, each person makes his own ברכה. If it was brought after the meal, one person makes the ברכה for everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two cases of wine at a group meal. It tells us who makes the ברכה in each case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine during the meal: each diner makes the ברכה for himself and does not rely on someone else. Wine after the meal: one person can make the ברכה and cover the whole group. The גמרא will explain the reason for this difference later.

keyTerms.meaning: During the meal (while people are still eating)
One person makes the blessing for everyone

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier rule in the משנה, that wine *before* the meal exempts wine *after* the meal. This line is about wine *during* the meal compared with wine *after* the meal, and about *who* makes the ברכה.

phrases.english: If wine came to them during the meal —
each and every one makes a blessing for himself.
If it came after the meal —
one person makes the blessing for all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's earlier rules about blessings at a meal
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine during the meal: each person makes his own ברכה. Wine after the meal: one person makes the ברכה for all.

steps.title: The one who blesses on the wine also blesses on the incense
steps.stepSummary: The person who made the ברכה on the after-meal wine also says the ברכה on the incense (מוגמר), even though the incense is only brought after the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he also says the ברכה on the incense, even though the incense is only brought after the meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that the person who blessed on the after-meal wine is also the one who says the ברכה on the incense for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In those days, fragrant spices were burned on coals after a meal so people could enjoy the smell. One might think the incense should be handled separately, since it only comes after the meal. The משנה says the same person who blessed on the wine also blesses on the incense.

keyTerms.meaning: Fragrant spices burned on coals after a meal for their pleasant smell

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with three rules. Wine during the meal: each person blesses for himself. Wine after the meal: one person blesses for all. That same person also blesses on the מוגמר.

phrases.english: And he says the blessing over the incense,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מְבִיאִין אֶת הַמּוּגְמָר
phrases.english: even though they do not bring the incense
until after the meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related rule to the after-meal wine case in Step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one who blesses on the after-meal wine also says the ברכה on the incense for everyone.

steps.title: Wine before the meal covers wine after it only on שבת and יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limits the משנה's earlier rule (wine before the meal exempts wine after it) to שבת and יום טוב. On other days, a person makes a ברכה on every cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The משנה taught this only about שבת and יום טוב, because then a person bases his meal on wine. But on the rest of the year's days, he makes a ברכה on each and every cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It goes back to the earlier משנה rule that wine before the meal exempts wine after the meal, and says this rule only applies on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given is that on שבת and יום טוב a person is קובע his meal on wine. He plans from the start to drink a lot, so his first ברכה covers all the wine that follows. On an ordinary day he did not plan to keep drinking, so each new cup is a fresh decision and needs its own ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
They only taught this rule about… (a phrase that limits the scope of a rule)
Sets or bases his meal (on something); makes it a planned, fixed part of the meal

steps.confusionAlert: This limit is NOT about the line just before it (wine during or after the meal). It refers back to an earlier line in the משנה: wine before the meal exempts wine after the meal.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one ברכה covers later food or drink only when the person planned it from the start. That idea comes up again and again in הלכות ברכות.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת וְיָמִים טוֹבִים,
phrases.english: They only taught this about Shabbatot and Festivals,
phrases.notes: "This" means the משנה's earlier rule that wine before the meal exempts wine after it.

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְאָדָם קוֹבֵעַ סְעוּדָּתוֹ עַל הַיַּיִן.
phrases.english: since a person bases his meal on the wine.
But on the rest of the days of the year,
he makes a blessing on each and every cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת וְיָמִים טוֹבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by limiting an earlier rule of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine before the meal exempts wine after the meal only on שבת and יום טוב. On weekdays, each cup needs its own ברכה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי agrees and adds more cases
steps.stepSummary: A second אמורא, רבי יהושע בן לוי, gives the same limit. He adds two more occasions when people plan their meal around wine: after the bathhouse and after bloodletting.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבה בר מרי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: The משנה taught this only about שבת and יום טוב, when a person comes out of the bathhouse, and at the time of bloodletting, because then a person bases his meal on wine. But on the rest of the year's days, he makes a ברכה on each and every cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel teaching that backs up רבי יוחנן's limit. It also widens the list of occasions where wine before the meal covers wine after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is the same: whenever a person sets his meal around wine, one ברכה covers it all. רבי יהושע בן לוי points out two more such times: after leaving the bathhouse, and after bloodletting, when people tend to drink a lot. This shows the rule depends on the person's plan, not on the calendar.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (introduces a parallel teaching that supports the previous one)

steps.whatToRemember: The real test is whether the person is קובע his meal on wine. שבת, יום טוב, after the bathhouse, and after bloodletting are all examples of that.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rabba bar Mari said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת וְיָמִים טוֹבִים,
phrases.english: They only taught this about Shabbatot and Festivals,
and when a person comes out of the bathhouse,
and at the time of bloodletting,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְאָדָם קוֹבֵעַ סְעוּדָּתוֹ עַל הַיַּיִן.
phrases.english: since a person bases his meal on the wine.
But on the rest of the days of the year —
he makes a blessing on each and every cup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's limit and adds more cases
steps.raayaObject: The limit that wine before the meal covers wine after it only when the meal is set around wine
steps.raayaSupportSource: A parallel teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי, passed on by רבה בר מרי

steps.title: רבא blesses twice on a weekday and is praised
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר מרי visited רבא on a weekday. He saw רבא make a ברכה on wine before the meal and again after it. He praised רבא and said this matches רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר מרי happened to come to רבא's house on a weekday. He saw him make a ברכה before the meal and then again after the meal. He said to him: Well done! And so said רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that shows the weekday rule being followed in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since it was a weekday, the wine before the meal did not cover the wine after it, so רבא made a new ברכה. רבה בר מרי, the one who passed on רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching, approves. This confirms that the limit from Steps 3 and 4 is the accepted practice.

keyTerms.meaning: On a weekday (not שבת or יום טוב)
Well done! (literally: may your strength be straight)

steps.whatToRemember: On a regular weekday, wine before the meal does NOT cover wine after the meal, so a new ברכה is needed. רבא did this, and it was praised.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר מָרִי אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רָבָא בְּחוֹל.
phrases.english: Rabba bar Mari happened to come to Rava's house on a weekday.
He saw him make a blessing (on wine) before the meal,
and then make a blessing again after the meal.
He said to him: Well done.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי.
phrases.english: And so said Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר מָרִי אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רָבָא בְּחוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that shows Step 4's teaching followed in practice
steps.raayaObject: On weekdays, wine after the meal needs its own ברכה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's practice, approved by רבה בר מרי in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: On a weekday, a person blesses on wine before the meal and again after the meal.

steps.title: רב יצחק בר יוסף questions אביי on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף saw אביי make a ברכה on every cup of wine on יום טוב. He asked why אביי did not follow רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר יוסף happened to come to אביי's house on יום טוב. He saw אביי make a ברכה on each cup of wine. He said to him: Doesn't the master agree with the teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second story, but it goes the other way from the last one. Here a guest is surprised that אביי made many ברכות on a day when one ברכה should have been enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי taught that on שבת and יום טוב, the ברכה on the first wine covers all later wine. אביי was making a new ברכה on every cup even though it was יום טוב. So it looks like אביי is going against רבי יהושע בן לוי, and the question sets up אביי's answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't the master agree with this?

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef happened to come
to the house of Abaye on a Festival.
He saw him make a blessing on each and every cup.
phrases.notes: Even though it was יום טוב, when people usually plan to drink wine through the meal.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
phrases.english: He said to him: Doesn't the master hold
by this teaching of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi?!
phrases.notes: Meaning the rule that on יום טוב one ברכה covers all the wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule. This one is the opposite case: יום טוב, yet many ברכות.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's practice of making a ברכה on every cup on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע בן לוי said that on יום טוב one ברכה covers all the wine, so separate ברכות look wrong.

steps.title: אביי explains he kept deciding anew to drink
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that he had not planned to drink more wine. Each cup was a new decision, so each one needed its own ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I change my mind (and decide to drink each time).
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why his practice does not go against רבי יהושע בן לוי. He did not plan his meal around wine, so every cup was a fresh decision.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule works because on יום טוב a person plans from the start to keep drinking. אביי did not have that plan. Each cup was a new decision (נמלך), so the first ברכה did not cover it.

keyTerms.meaning: changes his mind / makes a new decision

steps.whatToRemember: One ברכה covers later wine only when the person planned to keep drinking. If each cup is a new decision, each cup needs its own ברכה, even on יום טוב.

phrases.english: He said to him: I change my mind (each time).
phrases.notes: I did not plan to drink more. Each cup was a new decision.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction: the person did not plan to keep drinking
steps.terutzHavaAmina: On יום טוב, one ברכה always covers all the wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule depends on what the person planned. Someone who decides anew for each cup makes a new ברכה each time.

steps.title: Does wine during the meal cover wine after the meal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a ברכה on wine drunk during the meal covers wine drunk after the meal. Maybe it does not, because the two drinks serve different purposes.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: If wine was brought to them during the meal, does it exempt the wine after the meal? Even if you say that a ברכה on wine before the meal exempts the wine after the meal, that may be because both are for drinking. But here, one is for drinking and the other is to soften the food, so maybe not. Or perhaps there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. We already know that wine before the meal covers wine after it. Now we ask about wine during the meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine before the meal and wine after the meal are both drunk just to enjoy drinking. Wine during the meal is drunk to soften and wash down the food (לשרות). Maybe that difference in purpose means it cannot cover the after-meal wine, or maybe all drinking counts the same.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked before them
even if you say / if you conclude
or perhaps there is no difference

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. 'Before the meal' covering 'after the meal' is already accepted. The open question is only about wine drunk DURING the meal.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
If wine came to them during the meal,

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ שֶׁיִּפְטוֹר אֶת הַיַּיִן שֶׁלְּאַחַר הַמָּזוֹן?
phrases.english: does it exempt the wine after the meal?
Even if you say
that one who blessed on the wine before the meal
exempts the wine after the meal,
that is because this one is for drinking and that one is for drinking.
But here, where this one (after the meal) is for drinking,
and that one (during the meal) is to soften the food, maybe not.
Or perhaps there is no difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from wine before the meal to a new case: wine during the meal.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a ברכה on wine during the meal, which is drunk to soften food, cover wine after the meal, which is drunk for enjoyment?

steps.title: The אמוראים disagree: exempts or does not exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב and רב נחמן say the wine during the meal covers the wine after it. רב כהנא, רב ששת, רב הונא, רב יהודה, and all of רב's students say it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It exempts. רב כהנא said: It does not exempt. רב נחמן said: It exempts. רב ששת said: It does not exempt. רב הונא, רב יהודה, and all the students of רב said: It does not exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists the answers different אמוראים gave to the question. They split into two sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The side that says פוטר holds that all wine drinking at a meal is one kind of drinking. The side that says אינו פוטר holds that drinking to soften food is different from drinking for its own sake. Notice that רב's own students disagree with רב here.

phrases.english: Rav said: It exempts.
And Rav Kahana said: It does not exempt.
Rav Nachman said: It exempts.
And Rav Sheshet said: It does not exempt.
Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל תַּלְמִידֵי דְּרַב אָמְרִי: אֵינוֹ פּוֹטֵר.
phrases.english: and all the students of Rav say: It does not exempt.
phrases.notes: Even רב's own students disagree with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: פּוֹטֵר, וְרַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: אֵינוֹ פּוֹטֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answers to the question in Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is a disagreement. רב and רב נחמן say it exempts. רב כהנא, רב ששת, רב הונא, רב יהודה, and רב's students say it does not.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב נחמן from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the משנה, which gives separate rules for wine during the meal and wine after the meal. This seems to show that the wine after the meal needs its own ברכה, against רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב נחמן: If wine came to them during the meal, each person makes his own ברכה. After the meal, one person makes the ברכה for everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's view, that wine during the meal covers wine after it, using our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the משנה as one story: people drank wine during the meal and then drank wine after it. The משנה says a ברכה is made after the meal too, so the during-meal ברכה did not cover it. That would mean the answer is אינו פוטר, which is the opposite of רב נחמן.

phrases.english: Rava challenged Rav Nachman:
If wine came to them during the meal,
each and every person blesses for himself.
After the meal, one person blesses for everyone.
phrases.notes: רבא reads this as the same meal, so the after-meal wine still needs a ברכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks one side (רב נחמן) of the disagreement in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that wine during the meal exempts wine after the meal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires a ברכה on the after-meal wine even after wine was drunk during the meal, so the during-meal ברכה did not exempt it.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the משנה describes two separate cases
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the משנה's second line is a separate case: no wine was served during the meal, only after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what it means: If wine was not brought to them during the meal, but only after the meal, one person makes the ברכה for everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his view by reading the משנה differently from רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed the משנה describes one meal with wine both during and after. רב נחמן says these are two different meals. In the second case no wine was drunk during the meal, so of course a ברכה is needed afterward. The משנה therefore tells us nothing about whether during-meal wine covers after-meal wine.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it means (re-reading a source)

steps.whatToRemember: The question of wine during the meal stays a disagreement. רב נחמן survives רבא's challenge by reading the משנה as two separate cases.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what it means:

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא בָּא לָהֶם יַיִן בְּתוֹךְ הַמָּזוֹן
phrases.english: if wine did not come to them during the meal
but only after the meal,
one person blesses for everyone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the source as two separate cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה describes one meal with wine both during and after, so the after-meal wine needs its own ברכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second line of the משנה is about a meal with no wine during it, so it does not argue against רב נחמן.

steps.title: משנה: bread covers appetizers, but not the reverse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. A ברכה on bread covers the פרפרת, but a ברכה on the פרפרת does not cover bread. בית שמאי say: 'not even a cooked dish.' The next steps ask which line their comment refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he blessed on the bread, he exempted the פרפרת. If he blessed on the פרפרת, he did not exempt the bread. בית שמאי say: Not even a cooked dish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה, which it will now explain. This line sets up the coming discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread is the main food of the meal, so its ברכה covers smaller side foods like פרפרת. A side food is less important, so its ברכה cannot cover the main food, bread. בית שמאי's short comment, 'not even a cooked dish,' could attach to either line. The גמרא raises this question in the next step and never resolves it (תיקו).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of ברכות: the main food's ברכה covers secondary foods, but a secondary food's ברכה does not cover the main food.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּרַךְ עַל הַפַּת, פָּטַר אֶת הַפַּרְפֶּרֶת.
phrases.english: If he blessed on the bread, he exempted the appetizer.

phrases.aramaic: עַל הַפַּרְפֶּרֶת, לֹא פָּטַר אֶת הַפַּת.
phrases.english: If he blessed on the appetizer, he did not exempt the bread.
Beit Shammai say:
not even a cooked dish.
phrases.notes: It is unclear whether this goes on the bread line or the appetizer line. The next step raises this question.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּרַךְ עַל הַפַּת, פָּטַר אֶת הַפַּרְפֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the wine discussion and quotes the next part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread's ברכה covers פרפרת, but פרפרת's ברכה does not cover bread. בית שמאי say 'not even a cooked dish,' and it is unclear which clause they refer to.

steps.title: Which line do בית שמאי argue on? The first option
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether בית שמאי disagree with the first line or the second line of the משנה, and explains the first option. In that option, the תנא קמא says bread's ברכה covers both the פרפרת and a cooked dish. בית שמאי would say it does not even cover a cooked dish.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Do בית שמאי argue on the first line or the last line of the משנה? Maybe they argue on the first line. The תנא קמא says that a ברכה on bread covers the appetizer, and a cooked dish all the more so. בית שמאי come to say: it goes without saying that bread does not cover the appetizer. Bread does not even cover a cooked dish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is unsure which line of the משנה בית שמאי's comment belongs to. Here it lays out the first possibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has two lines: bread covers the פרפרת, and the פרפרת does not cover bread. בית שמאי's comment about a cooked dish could be attached to either line. If it goes with the first line, בית שמאי are saying that bread's ברכה is much weaker than the תנא קמא thinks: it does not even cover a cooked dish, and certainly not a פרפרת.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars (an open question)
The first clause of a source
The last clause of a source
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה
It goes without saying; this is obvious

steps.confusionAlert: In this first option, בית שמאי are not adding a new detail to the first line. They are disagreeing with it outright: they hold that bread's ברכה does not cover the פרפרת at all.

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
Do Beit Shammai disagree on the first clause,
or perhaps they disagree on the last clause?
For the first Tanna says:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּרַךְ עַל הַפַּת — פָּטַר אֶת הַפַּרְפֶּרֶת,
phrases.english: If he blessed on the bread, he exempted the appetizer,
and all the more so a cooked dish.
And Beit Shammai come to say:

phrases.aramaic: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא פַּרְפֶּרֶת דְּלָא פָּטְרָה לְהוּ פַּת,
phrases.english: It goes without saying that bread does not exempt the appetizer,
phrases.notes: In this option, בית שמאי reject the first line of the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ מַעֲשֵׂה קְדֵרָה נָמֵי לָא פָּטְרָה.
phrases.english: rather, it does not even exempt a cooked dish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אַרֵישָׁא פְּלִיגִי, אוֹ דִילְמָא אַסֵּיפָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to read בית שמאי's comment in the משנה line quoted in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether בית שמאי's cooked-dish comment refers to the bread clause or to the פרפרת clause.

steps.title: The second option: בית שמאי argue on the last line
steps.stepSummary: In the second option, the last line implies that the פרפרת's ברכה does not cover bread but does cover a cooked dish. בית שמאי would add that it does not cover even a cooked dish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe they argue on the last line, which teaches: if he blessed on the appetizer, he did not exempt the bread. That means bread is not exempted, but a cooked dish is. בית שמאי come to say that even a cooked dish is not exempted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second way to read בית שמאי. In this reading they are arguing about the weaker ברכה, the one on the פרפרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא's line about the פרפרת mentions only bread. That suggests the פרפרת's ברכה does cover a cooked dish. In this option בית שמאי accept the first line about bread and only argue on this implied point.

keyTerms.meaning: For it teaches (introducing a quote from the source)
Exempted; the ברכה covered another food

phrases.english: Or perhaps they disagree on the last clause,

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָתָנֵי: בֵּרַךְ עַל הַפַּרְפֶּרֶת — לֹא פָּטַר אֶת הַפַּת.
phrases.english: which teaches: If he blessed on the appetizer, he did not exempt the bread.
It is bread that he did not exempt,
but a cooked dish he did exempt.
phrases.notes: We learn this from the way the תנא קמא worded his rule.

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai come to say:

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ מַעֲשֵׂה קְדֵרָה נָמֵי לָא פָּטַר.
phrases.english: Even a cooked dish he also did not exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the question by laying out the second possible reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether בית שמאי accept the bread clause and argue only on the implication of the פרפרת clause.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו. It does not decide which reading of בית שמאי is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand: the question remains unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer and leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither reading is proven. So we do not know whether בית שמאי argue on the ברכה over bread or on the ברכה over the פרפרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question is left unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי's comment could refer to either line of the משנה. The גמרא leaves this as a תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from steps 13 and 14 without resolving it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Unresolved: we do not know which clause בית שמאי argue on.

steps.title: The משנה on sitting versus reclining
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and draws an inference from it: only reclining makes a joint meal, and sitting alone does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if they were sitting, each one blesses for himself, and so on. So if they reclined, yes, one may bless for all. If they did not recline, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and draws a careful inference from it. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה contrasts sitting, where each person blesses alone, with reclining, where one person blesses for all. From this the גמרא infers that only reclining joins people into one meal. This inference is what the ברייתא will seem to contradict.

keyTerms.meaning: They reclined (on couches, a formal way of eating together)

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ יוֹשְׁבִין כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: If they were sitting, each and every one, etc.
If they reclined, yes, it is a joint meal;
if they did not recline, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only reclining creates a joint meal, so that one person can bless for all.

steps.title: A ברייתא says sitting together is enough
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that travelers who sit down to eat have one person bless for all, even without reclining. This contradicts the inference from the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A contradiction is raised. Ten people walking on the road each bless for themselves, even if they all eat from one loaf. If they sat down to eat, one blesses for all of them, even if each eats from his own loaf. The ברייתא says 'they sat,' even though they did not recline!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to clash with the inference just drawn from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, sitting down alone is what turns the group into one meal. That goes against the משנה's implication that reclining is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted them; a contradiction between two sources

steps.confusionAlert: Eating from the same loaf does not join people. Only sitting down together for a meal does.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
Ten who were walking on the road,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכּוּלָּם אוֹכְלִים מִכִּכָּר אֶחָד —
phrases.english: even though they all eat from one loaf,
each and every one blesses for himself.
If they sat to eat,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד אוֹכֵל מִכִּכָּרוֹ —
phrases.english: even though each one eats from his own loaf,
one blesses for them all.

phrases.aramaic: קָתָנֵי ״יָשְׁבוּ״ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הֵסַבּוּ!
phrases.english: It teaches 'they sat,' even though they did not recline!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference drawn in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that only reclining creates a joint meal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets one person bless for all when they merely sat, so reclining should not be necessary.

steps.title: The travelers had planned to eat together
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the ברייתא is talking about travelers who said, 'Let's go eat bread at such-and-such a place.' Because they planned this, sitting together is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: the ברייתא means a case where they said, 'Let us go and eat bread in such-and-such a place.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק settles the contradiction by narrowing the case in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Agreeing ahead of time to eat at a set place gives the meal the same joint status (קביעות) that reclining gives. Without such a plan, the משנה's rule stands and reclining is required.

keyTerms.meaning: For example; in a case where

steps.whatToRemember: A group becomes one meal for ברכה purposes in either of two ways: by reclining together, or by sitting together after planning in advance to eat at a set place.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
In a case where they said,
'Let us go and eat bread in such-and-such a place.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: כְּגוֹן דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sitting by itself joins people into a meal, which would contradict the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sitting is enough only when the group planned in advance to eat at a set place. Otherwise reclining is required.

steps.title: רב's students plan a meal after his funeral
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells a story. When רב died, his students followed his funeral. On the way back, they said, 'Let's go eat bread by the נהר דנק.'
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב died, his students went after his casket. When they came back, they said: 'Let's go and eat bread by the Dannak River.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that connects to the topic we just learned: a group that plans ahead to eat together. This step sets the scene for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important detail is what the students said: 'Let's go eat bread at a certain place.' That is the same kind of planning statement that רב נחמן בר יצחק described in Step 18. The story will test whether that statement makes their meal count as a joint meal.

keyTerms.meaning: His soul rested (a respectful way of saying 'he died')
The Dannak River (the place they chose to eat)

phrases.english: When Rav died (literally: when Rav's soul rested),
his students went after him (following his casket).
phrases.notes: They escorted the funeral to where he was buried.

phrases.english: When they returned, they said:
Let us go and eat bread by the Dannak River.
phrases.notes: This is a planning statement, made before the meal began. Keep it in mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life story that matches the case רב נחמן בר יצחק described in Step 18: people who planned to eat together at a certain place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's students made a planning statement ('let's go eat bread at the נהר דנק') before eating together.

steps.title: Does planning make sitting count like reclining?
steps.stepSummary: After eating, the students asked a question. Does the משנה mean only real reclining makes a joint meal? Or does their earlier plan to eat together make simple sitting count like reclining?
steps.simpleTranslation: After they ate, they sat and had a question: Did the משנה say 'they reclined' specifically, so that just sitting does not count? Or maybe, since they said 'Let's go eat bread at such-and-such a place,' it counts as if they reclined?
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask a two-sided question about how to understand the word 'הסבו' (reclined) in the משנה. They need the answer to know whether one of them may bless for the whole group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: the משנה means real reclining, so sitting does not join them, and each person must bless on his own. Option two: saying 'let's go eat at a place' joins them, so sitting counts like reclining. The גמרא already gave רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer in Step 18, and it matches option two. But רב's students lived earlier and did not have that answer.

keyTerms.meaning: They ate (literally: wrapped, meaning ate bread)
They had a question (an open question)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the students forgot the meal. They are asking about ברכה: does their earlier plan make them one group, so that one person can bless for everyone?

phrases.english: After they ate,
they sat, and they had a question:
Did we learn 'they reclined' specifically,
phrases.notes: This refers to the line in the משנה from Step 16.

phrases.english: but if they only sat, no (it is not a joint meal)?
Or perhaps, since they said
'Let us go and eat bread at such-and-such a place,'
it counts as if they reclined?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the story from Step 19 into a halachic question about how to read 'הסבו' in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is reclining strictly required to make a joint meal, or does an earlier statement like 'let's go eat at a certain place' make sitting count like reclining?

steps.title: The students could not answer
steps.stepSummary: רב's students did not know the answer to their question.
steps.simpleTranslation: They did not have the answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The story tells us that the students could not answer their own question. Their teacher had just died, so they had no one to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ending is not a halachic ruling. It shows that the students were stuck. That helps explain why רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer in Step 18 matters: it settles the question רב's students could not answer.

keyTerms.meaning: It was not in their hands; they did not know the answer

steps.whyThisMatters: The halacha is decided by רב נחמן בר יצחק's explanation (Step 18): when people plan ahead to eat together, sitting together counts like reclining.

phrases.english: It was not in their hands (they could not resolve it).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells us the question from Step 20 stayed unanswered inside the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב's students could not decide whether their planning statement made them a joint meal.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה stands up
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה stands up. This starts the next part of the story.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה stood up.
steps.whatsHappening: This short line is a setup. The גמרא is about to tell us what רב אדא בר אהבה did and said in response to the students' question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing has been decided yet. The line only brings a new person into the story, and his reaction comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava stood up

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after the students fail to answer their question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup line: רב אדא בר אהבה stands, and his response follows on the next amud.
